messages:
ellie: Quick FYI — we rolled a small fractional canary of NCCL 2.19 to a subset of Dedicated H100 nodes in ap-southeast-2 and are seeing intermittent pod liveness restarts on ~6% of nodes. Not hitting the us-west canaries.

ben: Can you paste a log snippet and the exact node image/driver/kernel combo? How many pods/tasks affected in the wave?

ellie: Log snippet below (sanitized):
```
[2026-03-10T09:12:02Z] ncclCommAbort(): channel 3 timed out
[2026-03-10T09:12:02Z] ncclNetProbe: unexpected recv size 0
[2026-03-10T09:12:02Z] nvcuda: fault at 0x7fa12c, sigsegv
container exited with code 139
```
Node image: redwood/gpu-node:driver-535-kernel6.2.18-nccl-2.19.3
Node example: h100-dedicated-asp2-03
Affected: 3/48 tasks in this canary slice (~6.25%)

raj: That stack smells like a kernel <-> driver <-> NCCL edge case. Our compatibility matrix never validated kernel 6.2.18 with driver 535.86 + NCCL 2.19. Recommend pausing the phased rollout and rolling those canary nodes back to the last known-good image (driver-532 + kernel6.1 + nccl-2.18).

ops-oncall: @ellie please pause traffic to this canary wave and tag the wave state as "paused - investigating". Also open a low-touch customer notification for Dedicated reservations in ap-southeast-2.

ellie: Paused traffic at ~09:20Z and marked wave. Notifying support now.

jess: Rollback steps that we tested in staging: 
1) cordon and evict workloads from affected nodes
2) run `fleetctl set-node-image h100-dedicated-asp2-03 --image=redwood/gpu-node:driver-532-nccl-2.18-kernel6.1`
3) drain + wait for image rotation, then uncordon
4) run smoke: `./tools/check-nccl-liveness --region ap-southeast-2 --duration=30m`
Pinned stable image: `redwood/gpu-node:driver-532-nccl-2.18-kernel6.1`

maria: Heads-up: rolling back canary nodes will temporarily reduce available Dedicated capacity for customers in that AZ. Ops: estimate throughput hit and whether we should proactively migrate any reserved workloads to us-west1 while we stabilize. Note cost: cross-region migrations will add egress and potential preemption windows; notify sales if moving reserved GPU jobs.

ben: Dashboard: https://console.redwood.ai/dashboards/ops/nccl-liveness?from=now-6h
I've added an automated alert: canary failure rate > 3% for 10m. Current wave is ~6%.

ellie: Kicking off rollback now (rolling image rotation on four canary nodes). Will paste outputs.

sre-bot: [automated] Rollback job RB-0a7f queued by ellie at 2026-03-10T09:35:12Z — 4 nodes.

ellie: fleetctl output: "started image rotation for h100-dedicated-asp2-0[3-06], expected ready ~12-18m each"

jess: After nodes are back, run `nccl_tests/allreduce --size 256MB` from a test pod and tail for `ncclCommAbort` for at least 30m. If clean, proceed to mark wave as rolled-back.

ellie: Post-rollback smoke: by 09:57Z all 4 nodes rotated, smoke-run passed on 6 test pods, no ncclCommAbort in logs for last 40m. Affected tasks 0/48.

ops-oncall: Support + sales notified about the rollback and the service impact window (~09:20-09:57Z). Filed a postmortem card.

maria: I'll run a quick cost impact calc for the brief migration and share with finance.

ben: Action items: 1) add kernel 6.2.18 + driver 535.86 + NCCL 2.19 to compatibility CI matrix; 2) reproduce with heavy allreduce in staging; 3) when re-trying phased canary, start with tiny traffic fractions (1% -> 3% -> 10%) and include synthetic heavy-allreduce for the first 30m. Owners: raj (triage), jess (runbooks). ETA for triage: EOD tomorrow.

ellie: Leaving the wave paused until we have a reliable reproducer. I'll author the postmortem draft and link it here.

sre-bot: [automated] Incident INC-2026-0310 created by ellie and assigned to eng-infra — https://incidents.redwood.ai/INC-2026-0310

ben: Runbook update suggestion: include an explicit kernel-driver matrix check before any NCCL upgrade on Dedicated pools and inject a heavy allreduce synthetic workload as part of the first 30m of canary traffic.

ellie: Filed runbook PR: https://git.redwood.ai/runbooks/pull/482

jess: Closing thought: avoid full AZ/regional rollouts when node images deviate from baseline images. Thanks for the quick responses :thumbsup:
